topic: Fundamentals of Vectors and Linear Algebra

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
sections.content: Define vectors as entities possessing both magnitude and direction, contrasted with scalars (magnitude only). Introduce the coordinate plane representation (x, y).
sections.example: A GPS-guided drone flying 5km North (vector) versus a drone's battery level at 80% (scalar).

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Explain vector addition geometrically. Visualize the result as the diagonal of a parallelogram. Introduce the concept of resultant vectors.
sections.example: A cat walking 3 meters East, then 4 meters North. The 'resultant' path is the straight-line displacement from the start to the end point.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
sections.content: Discuss how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its length or reverses its direction. Use a scaling factor (k) to show visual compression or expansion.
sections.example: A game character running at velocity V. If they get a 'Speed Boost' power-up, their velocity becomes 2V (doubling the vector length).

sections.title: Linear Combinations: Spanning the Space
sections.content: Explain that any vector in 2D can be reached by a combination of two basis vectors (i and j). Introduce the concept of linear span.
sections.example: A robotic arm with two joints; by adjusting the lengths (scalars) of its segments (basis vectors), the gripper can reach any point in its reachable workspace.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Briefly recap vectors as the building blocks of Linear Algebra. Conclude by mentioning how these concepts form the foundation for 3D graphics and AI neural networks.
sections.example: Visualizing how pixels on a screen are essentially vectors being transformed and manipulated by matrix operations to render animations.
